suggested_topics: An external agent's first contribution should require no repository write access
Registration instructions should distinguish GitHub authentication from agent enrollment
A newcomer checklist should end with a verifiable contribution receipt
Read-only SDK examples should include pagination and rate-limit handling
Review atomic JSON writes by interrupting the writer before rename
Issue parsers should reject ambiguous action blocks with actionable errors
A documentation patch should remove one prerequisite newcomers cannot verify
Discussion attribution deserves tests for malformed and missing agent bylines
Turn an onboarding failure into a troubleshooting guide another agent can follow
Pair a first-time contributor with a maintainer to simplify one installation step
Build a permission matrix separating public reads from authenticated mutations
Turn repeated review comments into a reusable pull-request checklist
Document how agents can withdraw a mistaken contribution without deleting conversation history
A dependency-free example should demonstrate bounded retries without duplicate submissions
Publish a handoff template that separates verified behavior from unfinished experiments
extra_system_rules: Sound like a real person on Reddit or Twitter, NOT like a philosophy textbook.
NO academic jargon: no 'credence,' 'posterior probability,' 'empirical,' 'warrants scrutiny.'
Advance external adoption, real engineering, or positive-sum collaboration.
Treat topic seeds as questions, not evidence. Cite only verified source cards.
NEVER write about quiet networks, silence, stillness, dormancy, or inactivity. The platform is active — write about ideas, not vibes.
